title: Mock 5 · Full-Syllabus Check
blurb: A balanced full-syllabus check with a few medium numericals (butterfly, delta hedge, duration).

questions.q: SEBI introduced the Specialized Investment Fund mainly to:
options: Bridge the gap in portfolio flexibility between mutual funds and portfolio management services
Provide guaranteed returns to retail investors
Offer a tax-free alternative to ELSS
questions.explanation: Regulation becomes progressively more flexible from MF → PMS → AIF; SIF was created as a new product line under the MF Regulations to fill the MF–PMS gap.
hints: Correct — the workbook says SIF bridges the MF–PMS flexibility gap.
Wrong — AIFs continue to exist; SIF sits under the MF regulations.
Wrong — no SIF offers guaranteed returns.
Wrong — no SIF tax benefit is described.

questions.q: Which SIF strategy may dynamically invest across equity, debt, equity and debt derivatives, commodity derivatives, REITs and InvITs?
questions.explanation: Active Asset Allocator Long-Short: interval scheme, dynamic allocation across equity, debt, equity/debt/commodity derivatives, REITs and InvITs; short ≤ 25% of NAV.
hints: Wrong — Hybrid Long-Short covers equity, debt and their derivatives, with min 25% each in equity and debt.
Wrong — Sector Rotation is an equity strategy at sector level.
Correct — only the Active Asset Allocator strategy has this broad multi-asset mandate.
Wrong — Debt Long-Short invests in debt across duration.

questions.q: The appointment of an AMC can be terminated by a majority of the trustees or by what proportion of unitholders?
questions.explanation: AMC can be removed by a majority of trustees or 75% of unitholders; any change needs SEBI and unitholder approval.
hints: Wrong — a simple majority of unitholders is insufficient.
Wrong — two-thirds relates to independent trustees.
Wrong — 90% is not the threshold.
Correct — 75% of unitholders can terminate the AMC (subject to SEBI approval).

questions.q: What must an SIF include in its Investment Strategy Information Document (ISID) to show investors potential downside?
options: Scenario analysis depicting expected loss due to market movements
A ranking against peer mutual funds
questions.explanation: The ISID must contain scenario analysis depicting the expected loss to the investor due to market movements.
hints: Wrong — guarantees are not permitted.
Correct — SIFs must include scenario analysis of expected loss in the ISID.
Wrong — not a disclosure requirement.
Wrong — rankings are not allowed in advertisements, and not required here.

questions.q: AMCs must carry out additional due diligence on distributors who meet any of certain criteria. Which of these is one such criterion?
options: Commission of more than ₹10 lakh from one AMC
questions.explanation: Triggers: >20 locations; >₹100 crore non-institutional AUM; >₹1 crore commission p.a. industry-wide; >₹50 lakh from one AMC.
hints: Correct — multiple point presence (more than 20 locations) is a trigger.
Wrong — the threshold is 20 locations.
Wrong — the single-AMC threshold is ₹50 lakh.
Wrong — investor count is not a criterion.

questions.q: Over and above the base TER, brokerage and transaction cost for execution of trades in the cash market can be charged up to:
questions.explanation: Brokerage/transaction cost: up to 0.06% (cash market) and 0.02% (derivatives) of trade value, plus statutory levies.
hints: Wrong — 0.02% is for derivatives trades.
Wrong — not the current cap.
Wrong — far above the cap.
Correct — the cap is 0.06% for cash market trades.

questions.q: For income-tax purposes, which of the following is treated as a non-equity-oriented scheme?
options: A large cap fund holding 95% in listed Indian equity
A fund of funds investing in equity mutual fund schemes
An arbitrage fund with 70% in listed equity
questions.explanation: Equity-oriented = more than 65% of AUM in listed Indian equity shares; a FoF holds fund units, not shares, so it is non-equity-oriented.
hints: Wrong — more than 65% in listed domestic equity is equity-oriented.
Correct — FoFs investing in equity funds are non-equity for tax.
Wrong — ELSS invests at least 80% in equity.
Wrong — the 65% equity test is met.

questions.q: Up to what time can online redemption applications in overnight funds be submitted to get the closing NAV of the day immediately preceding the next business day?
questions.explanation: Overnight funds: redemption cut-off 3 pm, extended to 7 pm for online applications.
hints: Wrong — 3 pm is the general (offline) redemption cut-off.
Wrong — 1.30 pm is the purchase cut-off for liquid/overnight funds.
Correct — the cut-off for online overnight fund redemptions is extended to 7 pm.
Wrong — not the prescribed time.

questions.q: The platform hosted by CAMS and KFintech to help investors trace inactive and unclaimed mutual fund folios is called:
questions.explanation: MITRA is hosted by the two qualified RTAs and accessible via AMC, RTA, AMFI and SEBI websites.
hints: Correct — MITRA = Mutual Fund Investment Tracing and Retrieval Assistant.
Wrong — SCORES is SEBI's complaint system.
Wrong — debit freeze uses MF Central but is not a tracing platform.
Wrong — SMART ODR handles dispute resolution.

questions.q: A scheme's NAV rose from ₹20 to ₹23 over 6 months. What is the annualised return?
questions.explanation: Annualised return = simple return × 12 ÷ holding months.
hints: Wrong — 15% is the 6-month simple return.
Correct — simple return 15% × 12/6 = 30%.
Wrong — that compounds (1.15² − 1), which is not 'annualised' in the workbook's sense.
Wrong — that halves instead of doubling.

questions.q: Which risk-adjusted return measure must AMCs mandatorily disclose on their websites on a daily basis?
questions.explanation: IR = (Portfolio return − tier-I benchmark return) ÷ SD of excess returns (daily data); disclosed daily on AMC and AMFI websites.
hints: Wrong — Sharpe is widely used but not mandated for daily disclosure.
Wrong — Treynor is not mandated.
Wrong — Sortino is not mandated.
Correct — the Information Ratio is the only risk-adjusted measure mandated for daily disclosure.

questions.q: Which statement about passive (index) funds is correct?
options: They aim to beat the index through stock selection
They have higher expense ratios than active funds
They aim to replicate the index, have lower costs, and their key risk measure is tracking error
They are not affected by market falls
questions.explanation: Active funds try to outperform; passive funds track an index with low TER and are judged on tracking error.
hints: Wrong — that describes active funds.
Wrong — passive funds are cheaper (TER cap 0.90%).
Correct — passive funds mirror the index at low cost; tracking error matters.
Wrong — they fall with the index.

questions.q: Which derivative is described in the workbook as 'broadly a series of forward contracts' and is mainly traded OTC?
questions.explanation: Swaps exchange future cash flows by a prearranged formula; mainly OTC.
hints: Wrong — futures are single, standardised exchange contracts.
Wrong — options give a right, not an exchange of flows.
Wrong — an index fund is not a derivative.
Correct — a swap exchanges cash flows over time — a string of forwards.

questions.q: Under SEBI's October 2025 norms for derivatives on non-benchmark indices, the combined weight of the top 3 constituents must not exceed:
questions.explanation: Non-benchmark index derivative norms: ≥14 constituents; top ≤20%; top 3 ≤45%; descending weights.
hints: Wrong — 20% is the cap for the single top constituent.
Wrong — not the prescribed cap.
Correct — top 3 ≤ 45%, with top constituent ≤ 20% and at least 14 constituents.
Wrong — not the prescribed cap.

questions.q: How is the daily settlement price of an equity futures contract normally determined?
options: Opening price of the futures contract
Volume-weighted average price of the last 30 minutes of trading
Closing price of the underlying stock
Highest traded price of the day
questions.explanation: Daily settlement price: last-30-minute VWAP; final settlement price: closing price of the underlying on expiry.
hints: Wrong — the opening price is not used.
Correct — DSP is the VWAP of the last half hour (theoretical price if untraded).
Wrong — the underlying's closing price is used for FINAL settlement on expiry.
Wrong — the day's high is not used.

questions.q: Per SEBI's May 2025 circular, expiries of all equity derivative contracts of an exchange are limited to:
options: Only the last working day of the month
questions.explanation: NSE expiries fall on Tuesday (last Tuesday for monthly), BSE on Thursday; one weekly benchmark index option per exchange.
hints: Correct — each exchange chooses Tuesday or Thursday for all its equity derivative expiries.
Wrong — Friday is not permitted.
Wrong — the day is uniform per exchange.
Wrong — monthly contracts expire in the last week on the chosen day.

questions.q: A call option has a delta of 0.6. If the underlying rises by ₹5, the option premium will change by approximately:
questions.explanation: Delta = change in premium ÷ change in underlying.
hints: Wrong — that assumes delta of 1.
Wrong — that is the delta itself.
Wrong — a long call gains when the underlying rises.
Correct — 0.6 × ₹5 = ₹3, in the same direction for a call.

questions.q: All exchange-traded stock and index options in India are:
options: Exercisable at any time with physical delivery for index options
questions.explanation: Indian exchange-traded index and stock options are European; options are settled at the closing price on expiry.
hints: Wrong — American options allow early exercise.
Correct — they can be exercised only on the expiry day.
Wrong — Bermudan is not used for Indian equity options.
Wrong — index options are cash-settled.

questions.q: A trader buys a 500 call at ₹30, sells two 520 calls at ₹18 each and buys a 540 call at ₹10 (same expiry). What is the maximum profit per unit?
questions.explanation: Long call butterfly: max loss = net debit; max profit = strike gap − net debit; BEPs at 504 and 536.
hints: Wrong — 20 ignores the net premium.
Wrong — 4 is the maximum loss.
Correct — net debit = 30 + 10 − 36 = 4; max profit = 20 − 4 at expiry at 520.
Wrong — 36 is premium received only.

questions.q: A trader is short 6 lots of a call option (lot 100) with delta 0.5. How many lots of stock futures (lot 100) should he buy to be delta-neutral?
questions.explanation: Delta hedging: futures delta ≈ 1; long futures units = |option delta × units|.
hints: Correct — option delta = −0.5 × 6 × 100 = −300; futures delta 1 per unit ⇒ 300 units = 3 lots.
Wrong — that ignores delta.
Wrong — that doubles instead of halving.
Wrong — not supported by the arithmetic.

questions.q: A bond has a modified duration of 6. If its yield rises by 50 basis points, its price will change by approximately:
questions.explanation: Percentage price change ≈ −Modified duration × change in yield.
hints: Wrong — prices fall when yields rise.
Correct — %ΔP ≈ −MD × Δy = −6 × 0.5% = −3%.
Wrong — that assumes a 100 bp move.
Wrong — that is the yield change itself.

questions.q: According to BIS data quoted in the workbook, which class of derivatives has the largest notional amount outstanding globally?
questions.explanation: Interest rate contracts dominate both exchange-traded and OTC derivatives globally.
hints: Wrong — equity derivatives are far smaller.
Wrong — FX contracts are large but well below IRDs.
Correct — every business faces interest rate risk, so IRDs dominate.
Wrong — commodity contracts are the smallest.

questions.q: For cash-settled GOI bond futures, the final settlement price is based on:
options: The weighted average price of the underlying bond in the last two hours of trading on NDS-OM
The opening price of the futures contract on expiry day
The average daily FBIL overnight MIBOR for the month
questions.explanation: Bond IRF FSP: weighted average price of underlying in last 2 hours on NDS-OM; if fewer than 5 trades, FIMMDA/FBIL price.
hints: Correct — FSP uses the last two hours on NDS-OM; FIMMDA/FBIL price if fewer than 5 trades.
Wrong — the futures opening price is not used.
Wrong — that is for 91-day T-bill futures.
Wrong — that is for MIBOR futures.

questions.q: An investor buys one lot of a GOI bond put option (strike ₹98.50) at a premium of ₹0.20. At expiry the bond settles at ₹98.00. What is the net profit for the lot?
questions.explanation: Long put payoff = max(X − S, 0) − premium per ₹100 FV; multiply by 2,000 bonds per lot.
hints: Wrong — that ignores the premium paid.
Wrong — that uses 0.20 as the gain.
Wrong — that halves the lot.

questions.q: A trader expects short-term interest rates to rise. Using overnight MIBOR futures, the trader should:
questions.explanation: Rate-rise view: buy MIBOR futures, sell bond futures, buy bond puts, sell T-bill futures.
hints: Wrong — shorts gain when rates fall.
Wrong — bond calls gain when rates fall.
Wrong — bond futures gain when rates fall.
Correct — MIBOR futures are quoted as a rate, so a long position gains when rates rise.
